title: Flying to Bermuda with Louis Jordan's group
summary: His first flight took him to Bermuda for about a month with Louis Jordan and Charlie Gray, playing electric guitar.

bands.name: Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, somehow fishing made me think about that trip to Bermuda. Of course that was later, but --
Yeah. That's since I've been out here.
Yeah. You went with Louis Jourdan?
Louis Jourdan. Who else was in that group?
Who else was in that group?
Charlie Gray was on the drums.
Who was the bass player, then? They're both from Philadelphia, right?
Yeah. Monroe sang. He was a singer.
And -- oh, boy. You have got me now. I forget the names of them boys.
I ain't been with them all that time.
When did that gig go to Bermuda? Were you on tour, or did you go directly to Bermuda from L.A.?
Flew all the way to Bermuda?
Flew all the way to Bermuda.
That's a long trip to start out with.
You think it ain't? When I got into
Bermuda I had all these Bermudans, or whatever they call them, to meet the plane.
And they were all on bicycles. They were riding bicycles over there.
So they were the ones guided us to the place where the hotel was. Where we stayed.
How long did you play down there, a couple weeks?
Oh, yeah? It's nice down there.
Everybody down there was riding bicycles. Riding on the wrong side of the street. Instead of the right side, like we would ride on the right side, they'd ride on the wrong side.
They were digging the music, though.
Oh, yeah, they were digging it, dancing like we're dancing up here.
